chief_complaint: symmetric wrist and knuckle swelling, morning stiffness 2h
hpi_details: 35-year-old female presents with a 3-month history of symmetric pain and swelling in her wrists, MCP, and PIP joints of both hands. She reports profound morning stiffness that lasts up to 2 hours before she can fully use her hands.
ideas: She thinks the stiffness and swelling might be carpal tunnel syndrome or a repetitive strain injury from typing at her desk all day.
concerns: She is worried that her hand stiffness will prevent her from typing at her job and buttoning her young children's clothes in the morning.
expectations: She hopes to receive wrist splints and a strong anti-inflammatory prescription so she can use her hands without pain in the morning.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Early Rheumatoid Arthritis evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Early Rheumatoid Arthritis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes checking RF/anti-CCP, using NSAIDs for short-term symptom relief, and prompt rheumatology referral for DMARD therapy such as methotrexate, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: symmetric wrist and knuckle swelling, morning stiffness 2h
Key HPI features: A 35-year-old female presents with a 3-month history of symmetric pain and swelling in both wrists, MCP, and PIP joints, with morning stiffness lasting up to 2 hours.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Early Rheumatoid Arthritis.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Early Rheumatoid Arthritis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Osteoarthritis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Rapid symmetric joint swelling.
management_principles: Check RF/anti-CCP and inflammatory markers, use NSAIDs for short-term symptom relief, and refer promptly for DMARD therapy such as methotrexate
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: symmetric wrist and knuckle swelling, morning stiffness 2h

35-year-old female presents with a 3-month history of symmetric pain and swelling in her wrists, MCP, and PIP joints of both hands. She reports profound morning stiffness that lasts up to 2 hours before she can fully use her hands.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals normal. Bilateral wrists, MCPs, and PIPs are swollen (boggy), warm, and tender to palpation. DIP joints are spared. Decreased grip strength.
reference_soap.plan: Confirm synovitis and consider infection, crystal, viral, and connective-tissue causes; obtain RF, anti-CCP, ESR/CRP, CBC/chemistry, and baseline hand/foot imaging as clinically indicated. NSAIDs are only clinician-directed bridge therapy after renal, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, pregnancy, and interaction review. Rheumatology should select and monitor DMARDs after pregnancy planning/contraception counseling and baseline infection screening (including hepatitis and tuberculosis when immunosuppression is planned).

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Early Rheumatoid Arthritis
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Early Rheumatoid Arthritis
Implement evidence-based management plan: Check RF/anti-CCP, use NSAIDs for short-term symptom relief, and arrange prompt DMARD assessment

teaching.one_liner: Autoimmune synovial inflammation causing symmetric wrist and knuckle swelling with prolonged morning stiffness — early diagnosis and DMARD therapy prevent joint destruction.

must_ask.say: Are both wrists and hands affected equally?
How long does the stiffness last in the morning?
How long has this been happening?

history.answer: Both of my wrists and finger knuckles have been swollen and aching for the past few months, and my hands are so stiff every morning that I can barely use them.
It affects both of my wrists and the middle and base knuckles on both hands equally. The tips of my fingers feel completely normal.
It started gradually about three months ago and has been slowly and steadily worsening since then.
It is a constant dull, throbbing ache deep inside the joints, usually around a 4 or 5 out of 10, but it gets more painful when my hands are stiff.
Yes, my wrists and knuckles look puffy and swollen, and they feel warm to the touch, though the skin is not bright red.
When I wake up, my hands feel completely locked and stiff, and it takes up to two full hours of moving around before I can use them properly.
Gentle movement and running warm water over my hands help loosen them up, while resting too long makes the stiffness return.
Opening jars, turning keys, and typing at work have become very difficult, but walking and climbing stairs are completely fine.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
No, I have had no injuries, twists, or popping sensations in my wrists or fingers.
No, I have never had joint pain or swelling like this prior to three months ago.
I have been feeling noticeably fatigued and worn out lately, but I have not had any fever or unintentional weight loss.
No, I do not have any rash across my cheeks, scaly skin patches, or hair thinning.
No, my eyes are not red, gritty, or dry, and I have not had any dry mouth or oral ulcers.
No, I do not have lower back stiffness in the morning, heel pain, or swelling of my whole fingers or toes.
No, I have not had any recent diarrhea, burning with urination, discharge, or sore throats.
I do not eat large amounts of red meat or seafood, and I do not take water pills or diuretic medications.
No, I have never received steroid injections, joint surgery, or artificial joint implants.
I have been with my husband for eight years in a monogamous relationship, with no new sexual partners.

I thought maybe I developed severe carpal tunnel or strained my hands from typing so much at work. I'm really worried that my hands will get so stiff that I won't be able to type at work or even button my kids' clothes.
I'm hoping you can give me some wrist braces and strong pain relief so I can actually use my hands when I get up.
I have always been healthy and have no history of chronic medical conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I do not take any prescription medications, only occasional acetaminophen which does not help very much.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or environmental triggers.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only have an occasional glass of wine socially, perhaps once or twice a month.
I work as an office administrative assistant, and I live at home with my husband and young daughter.
My maternal aunt has rheumatoid arthritis, but neither of my parents has any autoimmune or joint diseases.
My last period was two weeks ago, my monthly cycles are regular, and there is no chance that I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/74 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Bilateral wrists, second through fifth MCP joints, and PIP joints are visibly swollen, boggy, and warm with marked tenderness upon palpation; DIP joints and thumbs are spared.
Bilateral hand grip strength is noticeably diminished secondary to pain and joint swelling; proximal upper extremity and lower extremity motor strength are intact at 5/5.
No malar rash, discoid lesions, psoriatic plaques, subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules, or tophi; fingernails appear normal without pitting or splinter hemorrhages.
Sclerae are non-icteric and without conjunctival injection, scleritis, or episcleritis; extraocular movements are full.
Oral mucosa is moist and pink without aphthous ulcers, mucosal erosion, or pharyngeal erythema.
Full cervical and thoracolumbar spine range of motion without spinous process tenderness or sacroiliac joint tenderness.
Gait is smooth, upright, and symmetric without antalgic limp or instability.
